items.title: Red Holloway interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: John Lee Hooker’s one. I mean he may say “Boom Boom Boom” but he’s got that voice and he’s got his type of rhythm that he can do that and get away with it.

ctx.x: If you can’t bend tones after somebody singing that, you know, God put the horn back in the case.

That’s right, that’s right, let me tell you. Oh Jimmy Witherspoon, I liked that line he got [sings] — I don’t like the way you been acting Mama — You know you ain’t treating me © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

right — You don’t have to go to the dentist tomorrow baby — Cause I’m knocking out your teeth tonight. But you see one of the things, when we write blues, there’s usually some kind of, it’s almost like a poem in a sense. If it doesn’t rhyme then the next phrase will rhyme and the next one after that, you know. And it always tells a story. Now there are a few exceptions to that rule, but they seem to still get over.
